facts.content: Patient presents with 3 days of diarrhea with vomiting and subjective fever.
facts.source_text: - Chief complaint: 3 days of diarrhea with vomiting and subjective fever.

facts.content: Watery diarrhea began 3 days ago and has become very loose.
facts.source_text: Patient reports onset of watery diarrhea 3 days ago which has become very loose.

facts.content: Patient has had at least four bowel motions today and has lost count of frequency.
facts.source_text: Frequency: lost count; at least four bowel motions today.

facts.content: Patient started vomiting this morning after breakfast, about 2 hours prior to the call.
facts.source_text: Vomiting since this morning (after breakfast, ~2 hours prior to call)

facts.content: Patient is unable to keep liquids down including water and tea.
facts.source_text: unable to keep liquids down (including water and tea).

facts.content: Patient reports subjective high temperature or fever without thermometer measurement.
facts.source_text: Subjective high temperature/fever (no thermometer used).

facts.content: Patient experiences intermittent periumbilical abdominal pain that is tender to touch and associated with strong urges to defecate.
facts.source_text: Periumbilical (around the navel) abdominal pain, tender to touch, intermittent and associated with strong urges to defecate.

facts.content: Patient passed urine about one hour prior to call.
facts.source_text: Passed urine about 1 hour prior to call.

facts.content: Patient reports no visible blood in stool or urine.
facts.source_text: No visible blood in stool or urine.

facts.content: Patient had contact with her brother who has had similar symptoms and believes 'everyone in school' has this.
facts.source_text: Patient reports contact with her brother who has had similar symptoms; reports that "everyone in school" has this.

facts.content: Patient has taken oral rehydration salts three times daily for the past two days but continues to vomit and symptoms are not improving.
facts.source_text: Tried oral rehydration salts (ORS, salt-sugar mix) three times daily for past two days but continues to vomit and symptoms not improving.

facts.content: Patient reports only usual menstrual cramps as past medical history.
facts.source_text: Past medical history: Not documented (patient mentions only usual menstrual cramps).

facts.content: Patient takes Vitamin D daily (dose, route, frequency not documented).
facts.source_text: - Vitamin D, dose/route/frequency not documented (patient takes daily).

facts.content: Patient uses Ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps (dose, route, frequency not documented).
facts.source_text: - Ibuprofen PRN for menstrual cramps, dose/route/frequency not documented.

facts.content: Patient has been taking oral rehydration salts about three times per day for two days.
facts.source_text: - Oral rehydration salts (ORS), taken ~3 times/day x 2 days.

facts.content: Allergies are not documented.
facts.source_text: Allergies: Not documented.

facts.content: Brother had similar recent symptoms of diarrhea and vomiting.
facts.source_text: Family history: Brother with similar recent symptoms.

facts.content: Patient is a non-smoker.
facts.source_text: Non-smoker.

facts.content: Patient drinks alcohol occasionally, described as 'a pint from time to time'.
facts.source_text: Drinks alcohol occasionally ("a pint from time to time").

facts.content: Patient lives with her brother and mother.
facts.source_text: Lives with brother and mother.

facts.content: Patient works as a graphics designer and is working from home today due to illness.
facts.source_text: Occupation: graphics designer; working from home today due to illness.

facts.content: Patient is not on contraception, not sexually active, and last menstrual period was 2 weeks ago.
facts.source_text: Not on contraception; not sexually active; last menstrual period 2 weeks ago.

facts.content: Assessment includes acute gastroenteritis likely infectious, probably viral due to household contacts, with 3 days of watery diarrhea, vomiting, subjective fever, and periumbilical abdominal pain.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute gastroenteritis, likely infectious (viral more likely given household contacts), 3 days of watery/loose diarrhea, vomiting, subjective fever, periumbilical abdominal pain.

facts.content: Assessment notes risk of dehydration due to ongoing vomiting and diarrhea and inability to retain fluids.
facts.source_text: 2) Risk of dehydration due to ongoing vomiting and diarrhea and inability to retain fluids.

facts.content: Assessment lists periumbilical abdominal pain likely related to gastroenteritis.
facts.source_text: 3) Periumbilical abdominal pain likely related to gastroenteritis; alternative causes not documented but should be considered if pain worsens or becomes focal.

facts.content: Arrange urgent in-person clinic appointment for assessment, vital signs measurement, and stool sample collection for microbiology.
facts.source_text: - Arrange urgent in-person clinic appointment for clinical assessment, measurement of vital signs, and collection of stool sample for microbiology (stool culture/enteric pathogen testing) as indicated.

facts.content: Advise patient to go to the Emergency Department urgently if symptoms worsen before clinic visit such as increased vomiting, high fever, severe abdominal pain, signs of severe dehydration, or bloody diarrhea.
facts.source_text: - If symptoms worsen before clinic visit (increased vomiting, high fever, severe abdominal pain, signs of severe dehydration, bloody diarrhea), go to the Emergency Department (ED) urgently.

facts.content: No antibiotics or antiemetics were prescribed during this consultation.
facts.source_text: - Medications: No antibiotics or antiemetics prescribed during this consult.

facts.content: Patient instructed to monitor stool frequency, presence of blood, fever, ability to keep fluids down, and urine output.
facts.source_text: - Monitoring: Monitor stool frequency, presence of blood, fever, ability to keep fluids down, urine output.

facts.content: Patient told to continue oral rehydration salts in very small frequent sips to minimize vomiting.
facts.source_text: - Patient instructions: Continue oral rehydration salts (ORS) in very small frequent sips to minimize vomiting.

facts.content: Patient advised to eat bland, simple foods if tolerated and avoid fruit, vegetables, and milk or dairy products while symptomatic.
facts.source_text: Take bland, simple foods if tolerated (toast, biscuits); avoid fruit, vegetables, milk/dairy while symptomatic.

facts.content: Patient instructed to avoid large boluses of fluid and instead take small, frequent sips.
facts.source_text: Avoid large boluses of fluid. Maintain small, frequent sips to preserve hydration.

facts.content: Plan to assess hydration status at in-person visit including vitals, orthostatic signs, mucous membranes, capillary refill, and urine output.
facts.source_text: - Assess hydration status at in-person visit (vitals, orthostatic signs, mucous membranes, capillary refill, urine output).

facts.content: If patient cannot tolerate oral fluids or shows moderate to severe dehydration, intravenous fluids will be administered in ED or clinic.
facts.source_text: - If unable to tolerate oral fluids or evidence of moderate-severe dehydration, administer intravenous fluids in ED or clinic as appropriate.

facts.content: Patient instructed to record urine output, dizziness, lightheadedness, orthostatic symptoms, skin turgor, and measured vitals.
facts.source_text: - Monitoring: Record urine output, dizziness, lightheadedness, orthostatic symptoms, skin turgor, and measured vitals.

facts.content: Evaluate abdominal pain in clinic or ED if it becomes severe, focal, or associated with peritoneal signs or persistent vomiting.
facts.source_text: - Evaluate in clinic/ED if pain becomes severe, focal, or associated with peritoneal signs or persistent vomiting.

facts.content: Patient may use ibuprofen as needed for menstrual cramps only at previously used dose.
facts.source_text: - Patient instructions: Use ibuprofen PRN for menstrual cramps/pain only as previously used (dose not documented);

facts.content: Urgent in-person clinic appointment to be arranged by support line.
facts.source_text: Urgent in-person clinic appointment to be arranged by support line (doctor arranged booking).
